_meta.purpose: Raw byte payloads for crates/eliot-types/tests/serde_t02_runtime.rs. Every value below is a JSON STRING holding the exact bytes a producer would emit or an attacker would present, never a pre-normalized object.
_meta.why_raw_bytes: Several acceptance cases (notably A5 duplicate keys, A8 unsupported versions, A12 ambiguous fallback, A14 malformed input) are only expressible as raw bytes. A json!/Value literal cannot hold a repeated key, cannot hold malformed JSON, and would normalize away the very bytes under test.
wire_facts: The workspace enables time with [local-offset, serde, serde-well-known] and NOT serde-human-readable, so a bare OffsetDateTime field serializes as, and deserializes from, a 9-element array [year, ordinal, hour, minute, second, nanosecond, offset_hours, offset_minutes, offset_seconds].

The workspace enables serde_json with [float_roundtrip] and NOT preserve_order, so a raw object member repeated in the bytes is a hard decoder error for a derived or manually-visited struct, while a repeated member collapsed into a serde_json::Value would be last-wins.
Fields carrying #[serde(with = "time::serde::rfc3339")] are RFC 3339 strings; '2026-09-23T12:00:00Z' has ordinal 266.
The workspace does not enable serde_json's preserve_order, so 'reordered' payloads below must stay byte-stable and are compared as text, not as ordered maps.
